CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right finger pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Sharon Brooks is a 48-year-old female presenting with right index finger pain. Patient reports injury occurred while skiing over the weekend (Sunday, approximately 4 days ago). While attempting moguls, patient's ski strap became caught on her finger, causing hyperextension or backward bending of the finger. Patient has attempted conservative treatment with ice application and ibuprofen, but continues to experience significant pain, particularly with movement. Pain is exacerbated with flexion and extension of the finger.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient reports recent constipation, otherwise not reviewed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Constipation
Appendectomy at age 18

MEDICATIONS
Miralax for constipation management
Ibuprofen as needed for pain

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is an active skier.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Right index finger examined. Tenderness noted over the distal phalanx (tip of finger) and over the distal interphalangeal joint. No tenderness over the proximal interphalangeal joint or metacarpophalangeal joint. Patient able to bend and extend finger with pain on flexion. Patient able to touch thumb with affected finger. No obvious deformity noted.

RESULTS
X-rays of right index finger: No fractures identified. Alignment normal. X-ray interpretation: Normal with no acute fracture.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Right index finger contusion on the tip of finger, without fracture.
- Fit aluminum foam splint for immobilization and protection
- Prescribe ibuprofen 600 mg every 6 hours for approximately 1 week for pain management
- Patient instructed to follow up if symptoms do not improve
